subject: Tenant crypto boundaries & operator profiles — VPC/on-prem DPA follow-up
messages:
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@medisphere.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: MediSphere Legal <legal@medisphere.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant crypto boundaries & operator profiles — VPC/on-prem DPA follow-up

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the call this morning — useful to align on the high-level. Please find attached our current DPA redlines (MediSphere_DPA_redlines_v3.pdf). Two immediate items from legal: 1) explicit guarantee that Redwood operators will not have regular access to customer plaintext data in private deployments, and 2) a clear subprocessors list with notification timelines.

A couple questions for the engineering proposal:
- In an on-prem deployment, can Redwood commit to never exfiltrating model inputs/outputs outside the customer's VPC without explicit written approval?
- For emergency "break-glass" scenarios, what is the minimum approval/process you need (ticketing + two-person approval?) and what audit evidence would we receive?

We'd also like a short bulleted summary of the KMS/BYOK options you support and any escrow tradeoffs. Can you respond by Friday so procurement can slot this into our vendor review?

Regards,
Alex Carter
Head of Security & Compliance
MediSphere, Inc.

Attachments: MediSphere_DPA_redlines_v3.pdf

Subject: RE: Tenant crypto boundaries & operator profiles — VPC/on-prem DPA follow-up

Alex — thanks for the redlines and for outlining the legal asks. Looping in Priyom (SRE/infra) and Lauren (legal) to propose concrete language and the engineering controls that map to the DPA.

Short answers up-front:
- Redwood's operating model for Private (VPC/on-prem) is designed to keep tenant data inside the customer's network. For BYOK, customers retain KMS control and we will not export plaintext keys.
- Break-glass: we can require a two-person approval flow for operator interventions; full session recording + immutable audit trail can be provided to the customer.

We'll follow up with a short technical proposal and suggested DPA language that addresses the operator scope, data egress guarantees, and subprocessor notification windows.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Tenant crypto boundaries & operator profiles — VPC/on-prem DPA follow-up

Team — technical proposal below (draft bullets we can give MediSphere):

1) BYOK modes we support:
   - Customer-hosted KMS (recommended): Redwood services authenticate with customer-managed short-lived certs; keys never leave customer KMS. No plaintext export.
   - Customer HSM with attestations: we can support an HSM-backed key where we store an encrypted key handle; attestation proofs available on demand.
   - Escrow option (customer-requested): hardware escrow with dual-control release (legal+engineering signoff).

2) Operator access profile:
   - Normal ops: no operator access to tenant plaintext or keys. Operators can view anonymized telemetry and aggregated metrics.
   - Emergency break-glass: operator can request scoped session; requires 2 approvals (SRE lead + customer contact). All actions recorded, session transcript, and a tamper-evident audit bundle delivered to customer (syslog + WORM storage pointer).

3) Data egress/cross-border controls:
   - No model inputs/outputs leave the VPC unless explicitly authorized in writing. For Dedicated hosted options we offer region pinning and contractual data locality.

4) Subprocessor handling:
   - Redwood will provide current subprocessor list (attached) and commit to 30-day notice for additions; critical subprocessors (storage, telemetry) will be listed with their role and locations.

Suggested DPA paragraph additions (short):
   - "Operator Access": Redwood will not access customer plaintext or encryption keys except under documented emergency procedures pre-authorized by the customer; all access is logged and delivered within X days.
   - "KMS Custody": Customer retains sole control of key material; Redwood is a custodian of encrypted kernel handles only and cannot reconstruct keys without customer authorization.

I'll attach the current subprocessor export for MediSphere's review. Happy to iterate.

Priyom
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_apr2027.csv

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@medisphere.com>, MediSphere Legal <legal@medisphere.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Tenant crypto boundaries & operator profiles — VPC/on-prem DPA follow-up

Alex / Legal team — attaching a concise set of items we propose adding to the DPA (bulleted below) and a proposed process for break-glass. Please confirm two things so we can finalize language and move to DocuSign:

1) Escrow approach: MediSphere preference between (A) escrowed HSM under dual-control release (requires physical release process) vs (B) attested customer HSM with key handles (software-only, faster). Each has different procurement impacts.
2) Permitted operator actions during break-glass: Do you require operator access to outputs for debugging, or do you prefer trace-based artifacts only (logs/metrics + sanitized transcripts)?

Proposed DPA bullets (summary):
- Data locality: Customer data remains in-customer VPC/on-prem unless explicit written permission to transmit.
- KMS control: Customer holds key material; Redwood acts on encrypted handles. No retention of plaintext keys.
- Operator access & break-glass: Two-person approval, time-limited session, immutable audit package delivered to customer within 5 business days.
- Subprocessors: Redwood provides current list and 30-day notice for additions; customer may object to critical subprocessors and require mitigation.
- Audit: SOC 2 Type II report available annually; evidence of operator sessions available on request under NDA.

Links: short proposal doc in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-MediSphere-DPA

Can we block 30 minutes on Friday 2027-04-30 at 11:00 PT for quick alignment? If that works for you, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@medisphere.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: MediSphere Legal <legal@medisphere.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Tenant crypto boundaries & operator profiles — VPC/on-prem DPA follow-up

Naomi / team — appreciated the clear bullets. Quick answers: 

1) Escrow: procurement prefers option (B) attested customer HSM with key handles if it provides equivalent assurances — faster procurement cycle and avoids physical escrow logistics. We'll need attestation artifacts during onboarding.
2) Break-glass: legal prefers operator access to sanitized outputs (trace artifacts + sanitized transcripts) by default; allow full output access only when a signed statement from our security officer is provided per-incident. Two-person approval + logged session is acceptable.

We're good to move forward with those bullets; please prepare updated DPA language and procurement checklist. I'll ask procurement to circulate required fields and see if DocuSign can be queued once we get the updated DPA.

Yes to the Friday 11:00 PT sync — please send invite.

Regards,
Alex Carter
Head of Security & Compliance
MediSphere, Inc.
